formula_or_derivation: Per county, 2022-2024: weighted total = orange days×1 + red days×1.5 + purple days×2 + maroon days×2.5 (days by 24-hour PM2.5 AQI category); weighted average = total ÷ 3. Metro rank = rank of the highest county weighted average in the metro.

formula_or_derivation: Metro rank = rank of the highest county annual PM2.5 design value (µg/m³, EPA, 2022-2024) in the metro. A design value is the concentration calculated in the form of the national air quality standard (EPA).

True = reference-grade monitor; False = air sensor ("low-cost sensor"). OpenAQ Docs define the field as whether the device is used for official monitoring. OpenAQ Explorer describes reference-grade monitors as the "gold standard" for measuring pollution concentrations, typically run by government agencies for regulatory purposes; air sensors are less sophisticated instruments that are small, portable and affordable, so institutions and individuals can deploy them to fill gaps in air quality knowledge. In Step 1, all 102 reference sensors are AirNow "Government Monitor" instruments; the 719 low-cost sensors are Clarity, AirGradient and BEACO2N devices.
